Hi Carlos. The European auditor is visiting your office next month. Can I ask you some questions?
Of course, Emma. I am available now.
Thank you. Can your team provide the maps of all the farms?
Yes, we can. The maps are ready in the IMS system.
Great. Can you translate the reports into English?
I can translate the short reports, but I can't translate the long ones this month.
That's OK. The team in Geneva can do the long reports. Can you speak with the auditor in English?
Yes, I can, but I can't speak fluently yet. I can explain the criteria slowly.
That's perfect. Auditors like clear answers, and your skill with the data is very good.
Thank you, Emma. I can send you the documents tomorrow.

My English is getting better every week. Today I can read a sustainability report in English, and I can write a short email to a colleague. I can present the numbers of our farms in a meeting, slowly and clearly. But I can't speak fluently yet, and I can't understand fast speakers on a call. When I can't understand, I say: Can you repeat that, please? My goal for this year is simple. In December, I want to explain the EUDR to a buyer without help.

Hi Carlos, this is Grace from Kigali. Thank you for your email. Good news: the buyer can visit on Thursday, not on Wednesday. So you can join the call on Thursday at ten in the morning, Brazil time. I can present the Rwanda results, and you can present the Brazil results. About the supplier form: no problem, your manager can sign it next week. Thank you, and see you on Thursday.

First, I read the six requests from Grace. Then, I say yes: I can send the EUDR maps today. Next, I explain: I can translate the checklist, but I need two days. After that, I say no politely: I can't sign the supplier form. Finally, I ask a question: can I join the call on Thursday?
